statBlock.name: Werebear
statBlock.speed: 30 ft. in humanoid form. 40 ft., climb 30 ft. in bear or hybrid form.
statBlock.description: A reclusive guardian that takes bear form to defend its territory. It favors claws or an axe over a bite that could spread its curse.

sections.Armor: AC 10 in humanoid form. AC 11 from natural armor in bear and hybrid forms.
sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Languages: Common. It cannot speak in bear form.
sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action, polymorph into a Large bear, a Large bear-humanoid hybrid, or its true humanoid form. Size and armor class change with the form. Worn and carried equipment stays as it was. Death returns it to its humanoid form.
Keen Smell. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on smell.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. In humanoid form, make two Greataxe attacks. In bear form, make two Claw attacks. In hybrid form, choose either pair.
Bite (bear or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage. A humanoid target that is not already a lycanthrope makes a DC 14 Constitution save or contracts werebear lycanthropy.
Claw (bear or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Greataxe (humanoid or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (1d12 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Player lycanthropy:
A character keeps its own statistics except for the changes listed here. It gains the printed nonhumanoid speeds, damage immunities, traits, and actions that require no equipment, plus proficiency with the lycanthrope's natural attacks. Use the listed natural weapon damage. The character cannot speak in animal form.
Only a humanoid that is not already a lycanthrope saves against the curse when hit by a curse-bearing attack. The Constitution save DC is 8 + the attacking lycanthrope's proficiency bonus + its Constitution modifier. A character who resists the curse keeps their usual alignment and personality in humanoid form. The full moon forces them into animal or hybrid form until it wanes. A character who embraces the curse acquires the lycanthrope's alignment and can eventually learn to shift at will. The DM can take control of the character until the curse is removed. Remove Curse can end an acquired curse. A natural-born lycanthrope needs Wish.
Raise Strength to 19 if lower. Bear and hybrid forms gain +1 AC from natural armor. Use Strength for natural weapon attack and damage rolls.
sections.Nonhuman lycanthropes: The printed blocks assume a human. For a lycanthrope of another ancestry, the DM can retain one or more traits from its humanoid form, such as Fey Ancestry for an elf.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 206–207 and 208. The player sidebar erratum clarifies curse eligibility. The profiles apply that limit to the curse-bearing attacks. Immunity wording follows the global errata.

statBlock.name: Weretiger
statBlock.speed: 30 ft. in humanoid or hybrid form. 40 ft. in tiger form.
statBlock.description: A solitary hunter that prefers the scimitar or longbow in humanoid form and can pounce in tiger or hybrid form.

sections.Languages: Common. It cannot speak in tiger form.

Scimitar (humanoid or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Longbow (humanoid or hybrid only). Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

statBlock.name: Troll (Loathsome Limb; Severed Arm)
statBlock.description: A detached troll arm that crawls and lashes out under its parent’s direction.

sections.Severing and reattachment:
When the troll takes 15 or more slashing damage from a single instance, roll a d20. On 1–10 no part is severed. On 11–14 it loses a leg if any remain. On 15–18 it loses an arm if any remain. On 19–20 it is decapitated. It survives the decapitation if it can regenerate. If the troll dies after decapitation, its severed head also dies.
A detached part acts on the troll’s initiative with its own movement and action. If the troll finishes a short or long rest before reattaching the part, a replacement grows and the old part dies. The sidebar gives no reattachment action or timing.
sections.Traits: Regeneration. The part regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. Acid or fire damage prevents that healing at the start of its next turn. Applying the troll’s Regeneration to the part, it dies when it begins its turn at 0 HP and cannot regenerate.
sections.Actions: Claw. Make one Claw attack on the arm’s turn using the parent Troll’s attack. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. The attack has disadvantage unless the troll can see both the arm and its target.
sections.Effects on the troll: Each lost arm removes one Claw attack from the troll’s Multiattack. Losing its head removes Bite, and the body is Blinded unless the head can see it. With one leg missing, halve the troll’s speed. With both legs missing, it falls Prone and can crawl if it has one or both arms. Halve its speed if it has only one arm to crawl with. With no arms or legs left, its speed is 0 and speed bonuses cannot increase it.
sections.Parent encounter: Use this procedure only with the Troll (variant). The sidebar gives each part its own AC, HP, movement and any listed attack. It gives no separate size, ability scores, challenge rating or XP. The DM decides how to resolve checks or saves the sidebar leaves unspecified.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 291, Loathsome Limbs sidebar and the Troll’s Regeneration.
